basis.text: The licence looked up is ABC Type 48 (on-sale general, public premises), as stated in the description.

A Type 48 licence is an on-sale general licence. State law limits these to one for each 2,000 inhabitants of the county; in a county over that number ABC issues no additional one, so the licence comes by transfer of an existing licence unless state law allows otherwise.
Census tract 106.00: 52 active on-sale retail licences in ABC's licences as they stood on 16 March 2022, against 12 authorised in ABC's census tract authorisations of September 2026.

The tract is over its authorised number. State law tests a new licence and a transfer from other premises for undue concentration, and the applicant does not say how the liquor licence will be obtained.

The description does not give how the liquor licence will be obtained (new, or a transfer from another owner or another location), so the rules cannot say which licence rules apply: insufficient information.

Licences with an unknown status on 2022-03-16: 19 ABC licences within 1,000 ft and 15 in the census tract were on file, but ABC's daily reports do not show their status that day (it changed two or more times since). They are left out of the licence counts, the census tract count and what the space is read as.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Bar with Limited Live Performance at 253 Columbus (35 m away, NCD-BROADWAY), an agency referral from 2018 approving LLP as accessory to an existing bar use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved live entertainment accessory to a bar at 253 Columbus (one door away), citing that bar is a permitted conditional use in Broadway NCD. As an agency referral, it shows Planning's willingness to support entertainment in existing bars on this block, though it does not test a full CUA hearing for a new bar use.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Restaurant with Place of Entertainment permit at 515 Broadway (34 m away, NCD-BROADWAY), an agency referral from 2021 approving nighttime entertainment accessory to an existing restaurant.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a POE permit for a restaurant on the same block in 2021, confirming that nighttime entertainment remains acceptable in NCD-BROADWAY when accessory to food service. This concept proposes entertainment as primary to a bar, which may require a full CUA hearing.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: ABC Type 48 referral at 527 Broadway (23 m away, NCD-BROADWAY), approved 2019 for continuation of established bar use (Specs Twelve Adler Museum and Cafe).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 48 license continuation for an established bar at 527 Broadway in 2019, confirming that bar use is principally permitted in NCD-BROADWAY. As a continuation (not a new use), it does not test whether a change from restaurant to bar would be approved.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA at 463–473 Broadway (112 m away, NCD-BROADWAY), filed 2001, approved to expand an existing bar from 2,500 to 4,300 square feet. This is a use decision showing Commission approval of bar expansion in the district.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved a bar expansion on Broadway in 2001, demonstrating that bar uses can be approved in NCD-BROADWAY when presented to the Commission. However, it was an expansion of an existing bar (not a change from restaurant to bar), and the approval was 21 years ago.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA at 493 Broadway (91 m away, NCD-BROADWAY), filed 2015, approved in 2016 to convert vacant adult entertainment and bar uses to a new restaurant with Other Entertainment use.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved a restaurant with entertainment use in 2016 on Broadway, showing willingness to support food-and-entertainment concepts in the district. The approval took 11 months (filed May 2015, decided April 2016), illustrating typical CUA timelines for entertainment uses.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: CUA at 644 Broadway (145 m away, CCB district), filed 2016, approved in 2016 to change from movie theater to Other Entertainment (theater) with bar use for alcohol sales during performances.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: The Commission approved a bar use in conjunction with entertainment at a nearby venue, taking 5 months from filing to decision. This shows the Commission's openness to entertainment-plus-bar concepts in the immediate area, though CCB zoning is more permissive than NCD-BROADWAY.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Place of Entertainment agency referral at 1155 Grant (92 m away, CCB district), approved 2019 for POE accessory to an existing bar (Bow Wow Cocktail Lounge).
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning routinely approves POE permits as accessory to bars in the immediate neighborhood through agency referrals, but this is in CCB where bar use is permitted, not NCD-BROADWAY where bar requires conditional use.

filing_playbook.action: Engage an architect, acoustical consultant and kitchen/mechanical engineer to prepare preliminary plans and a sound-attenuation strategy before filing the CUA.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Commission an acoustic baseline study of the space and adjacent residential units, and design soundproofing measures (wall/ceiling insulation, vibration isolators, door seals, PA limiters) sufficient to meet Entertainment Commission standards. Have the architect prepare scaled floor plans showing the bar layout, seating, performance area, kitchen and restrooms, and the mechanical engineer assess the existing hood and grease interceptor. These documents support the CUA application and will be required for the building and health permits.

timeline_cost.notes: These figures are the time and government cost to obtain the four approvals in the entitlement path (Conditional Use Authorization, Place of Entertainment permit, Health permit to operate, and Building permit with change of use) when they are granted. The timeline runs from forming the entity to receiving all four approvals: 8.5–24 months. The cost range includes government fees only (CUA $3,100–$15,000; POE permit $2,708; health plan check $828–$2,207 and permit $470; building permit $800–$15,000; plus business registration $55–$700, state entity formation $70–$150, sellers permit $0, EDD registration $0, food safety manager $100–$250, RBS training $50–$360 for 12 staff, fire Place of Assembly $446, FOG program $0–$500, sign permit $300–$1,500, and music licenses $600–$5,000 per year); it does not include the cost of purchasing the ABC Type 48 license ($17,000 minimum for a newly released quota license, $100,000–$450,000 for a transferred license on the open market in San Francisco as of 2022), nor the 120–300 day ABC transfer timeline, nor any professional fees (architect, acoustical consultant, license broker, attorney). The timeline assumes the CUA is approved on first hearing (4–6 months after filing) and the POE permit is approved at the first Entertainment Commission hearing (3–4 months after CUA approval); the building permit and health permits follow construction and final inspections (2–6 months). A CUA denial, a continued hearing, or a discretionary review request would extend the timeline by 3–12 months. The timeline does not account for withdrawal, denial or cancellation; the decision times block shows that two of five dated NCD-BROADWAY bar/restaurant use decisions were withdrawn (no time to approval for those cases).

status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

records_summary: 270 Columbus Ave sits in the Broadway Neighborhood Commercial District (NCD-BROADWAY) where a Bar use on the first story and basement is a conditional use requiring Planning Commission approval. The site history shows continuous bar and restaurant operations since at least 2002, with a fast-food restaurant conditional use approved in 1985, followed by multiple approvals for full bar and full-service restaurant uses, and a Place of Entertainment permit approved in 2006. The block is extremely dense: 49 registered food and drink businesses within 500 ft (18 of them bars), 33 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, and 106 licenses within 1,000 ft, triggering ABC's undue-concentration flag.
data_gaps: No text of hearing conditions or commissioner discussion for the 1985 fast-food CU (Motion 10438) that is still referenced in the 2002 continuation approval
